panel.noMore: There is no more help for this field.

haFencing.alt: HA diagram: when a node dies, it is cut off (fenced) and its VMs start again on another node.
haFencing.note: Fencing stops a node we think is dead from running the
haFencing.note2: same VM at the same time and corrupting its disk.

backupChain.alt: Backup diagram: the first backup copies everything; later ones add only what changed (incremental).
backupChain.restore: Restore = full + the increments after it
backupChain.note: Longer chains: faster, smaller backups but slower restores.

replicationDr.alt: Replication and DR diagram: VMs at the main site are copied to a standby site on a schedule and started there in a disaster.
replicationDr.note: A shorter schedule means less data lost in a disaster (RPO).
replicationDr.note2: Run a test now and then to check the copies start.

sdn.alt: SDN diagram: VMs on several nodes join one virtual switch; a virtual router sends traffic out with SNAT; a public IP brings traffic in.
sdn.note: VMs share one private network on any node.

securityGroup.alt: Security group diagram: incoming connections reach the VM only if a rule allows them; outgoing connections are allowed by default.
securityGroup.note: Rules are set separately for incoming and outgoing traffic.
securityGroup.note2: Incoming connections with no matching rule are blocked.

placement.alt: Placement diagram: 'together' keeps VMs on the same node; 'apart' keeps them on different nodes.
placement.note: 'Must' rules block the start if broken; 'prefer' rules apply when possible.

storageSharing.alt: Storage diagram: local storage is separate on each node, so moving a VM copies its disk; shared storage is used by all nodes, so only memory moves.
storageSharing.note: HA restarts on another node need shared storage.

thinOvercommit.alt: Thin provisioning diagram: three VMs are promised 60 GiB each but the real disk is 100 GiB; each uses only what it writes.
thinOvercommit.promised: Size promised to VMs (180 GiB total)
thinOvercommit.note: Disks use only what they write, so you can promise more than you have.
thinOvercommit.warn: If the real disk fills up, VMs cannot write and pause.

liveMigration.alt: Live migration diagram: the VM keeps running while its memory is copied, changed pages are sent again, then it pauses briefly and continues on the new node.
liveMigration.step1: Send all memory while it runs
liveMigration.step3: Pause very briefly and continue on the new node

declarativeApply.alt: Manage-as-code diagram: the YAML file is compared with the cluster to show what will be added, changed and removed; applying makes the cluster match.
declarativeApply.note: The file is the 'wanted state'; applying makes the cluster match it.
declarativeApply.note2: If someone changes it in the UI, you see 'differs from file'.

dedupStore.alt: Backup store diagram: three backups repeat the same pieces, but the store keeps each different piece only once.
dedupStore.note: Identical data is stored once, so many backups take little space.
dedupStore.note2: Clean-up (GC) removes pieces no backup uses.

quorum.alt: Voting diagram: with two of three nodes up there is a majority, so the cluster keeps running.
quorum.note: With 2 nodes, losing one breaks the majority and stops.
quorum.note2: Use 3 or more nodes, or a vote-only node (witness).
